text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- East Timor Bishop Carlos Belo and self-exiled political leader Jose Ramos Horta received the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize on Tuesday. They thanked for the honour by calling on Indonesia to free political prisoners in the Indonesia-ruled territory of East Timor.
- Prime Minister Torbjoern Jagland met the opposition in parliament late on Tuesday after the Nobel Peace Prize banquet to discuss ways of finding agreement on the 1997 state budget.
- Since 1967 infant mortality has been reduced by almost 70 percent in Norway.
- Aker Stord demands 518 million crowns from Norsk Hydro for extra work during the construction of the Njord offshore platform.

- Finance Minister Jens Stoltenberg have suggested to cut the Norwegian Space Centre's grant by 32 million crowns and has asked the company to postpone investments on the Arctic island of Spitzbergen. In his previous job as industry Minister, Stoltenberg was for investing more on Spitzbergen.
- Unilever/GB Glace lost 65 million crowns from 1991 to 1995 in attempts to market ice cream in Norway. Norway is the only European country where the company is not selling ice cream.
